original_test_intent: Verify that the approved BMC user can enroll the supported two-factor method and subsequently authenticate with username/password plus a valid current second factor to reach Overview, while preserving account security and a recoverable management path.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/SUT/firmware, test account and role; prove an independent recovery administrator or physical console before enrollment; verify BMC and authenticator clocks without exposing secrets; authorized operator opens 2FA, scans the QR directly into the approved authenticator and secures the backup code; record only redacted enrollment state; log out, start a fresh session, enter password and one current code privately, and record successful Overview navigation plus audit/session events; leave enrollment in the owner-approved final state.
manual_activity: The authorized user privately scans the QR code, stores the recovery code, enters credentials and TOTP, observes Overview and retains control of every secret; the agent may organize only redacted evidence.
required_inputs: Dedicated test account, role and approved final enrollment state
Authenticator device/application, BMC/authenticator time synchronization and allowed TOTP window
Independent recovery administrator or physical-console procedure verified before enrollment
safety_requirements: Never capture, transmit, store or echo password, QR image, TOTP seed, backup code or OTP value
Use a noncritical test account unless engineering explicitly approves another identity
Verify recovery access and clock synchronization before changing authentication state
Do not weaken TLS, disable other protections or use shared browser/session artifacts
Stop after an unexpected enrollment/login failure or lockout warning; do not brute-force or automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate non-secret identity, account role, factor policy, recovery readiness and clock status
Guide the operator through approved UI checkpoints without viewing secrets
Collect timestamps, redacted enrollment status, Overview navigation and audit/session evidence
Do not scan QR, generate/store TOTP seed, enter credentials/OTP, disable 2FA, retry login automatically or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve test account/role, factor method, TOTP tolerance and final enrollment state
Approve backup-code custody, failed-attempt limit and recovery procedure
Review redacted evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its prose matches the high-level workflow, but there is no safe autonomous command: enrollment secrets and the OTP must remain operator-controlled.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the supported BMC WebUI with the operator privately handling QR, backup code, password and TOTP; automation may only validate non-secret page state and collect redacted audit evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The five-minute enrollment/login flow and correct-code-to-Overview criterion remain; account, factor and recovery parameters require approval.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a dedicated account and private operator factor handling, verify one fresh second-factor login, and retain only redacted state/navigation/audit evidence with tested recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds account isolation, time synchronization, secret-redaction, attempt limits, recovery proof and final-state ownership.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A QR display, enrollment flag, API response or password-only session cannot prove the required password-plus-valid-factor login to Overview.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Screenshots, browser recordings and automation traces can leak reusable seeds or backup codes; clock skew can cause false login failures and repeated attempts can lock the account.

project_override_considerations: Engineering should decide whether an invalid/expired-code negative check is required; it is not explicit in the source and must not be added if it risks lockout. The final enabled/disabled state must be stated.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/firmware, test-account role and non-secret pre-enrollment state
Recovery-path verification and redacted factor-policy/clock evidence
Operator attestation that QR/seed/backup code/password/OTP remained private
Fresh-session timestamp, valid-factor success and Overview navigation without secret values
Redacted BMC authentication/audit events, final enrollment state, recovery record and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The unique source consistently requires 2FA enrollment and valid-code login. Missing project account/factor/recovery details are prerequisites, not contradictory source identity.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The 2FA purpose and operator boundary are clear. Account, authenticator, recovery and policy inputs can be supplied; execution remains confirmation-gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2213 Wistron-BMC-01063-V002: approve the BMC/firmware-supported 2FA method, dedicated test account/role, authenticator and TOTP time/window policy, backup-code custody, maximum failed attempts and whether any invalid/expired-code negative check is required, independent administrator/physical recovery, redaction/audit requirements and final enabled/disabled enrollment state.

review_improvement: Makes the QR/TOTP secret boundary explicit, prevents credential leakage and lockout, and turns successful Overview navigation into auditable non-secret evidence with recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: TOTP enrollment exposes a long-lived seed through the QR code; anyone who records it can reproduce future codes, so screenshots and automation traces are a security failure even if login succeeds. A valid result also depends on BMC/authenticator clock alignment and a fresh session actually enforcing the second factor. Recovery must be proven before enrollment because the factor or backup code can be lost. One successful login is enough for the stated positive criterion; adding repeated or negative attempts without approval increases lockout risk rather than coverage.
